messages:
maria p: Noticed a strange spike in validation noise for function hooks in prod canary slice. ~1.8% soft_rejects and 0.3% hard_rejects this morning. Customers seeing ambiguous 5xx and no example payloads.

ton y l: dropping a concrete example from logs:
```json
{
  \"action\": \"turn_on\",
  \"args\": [\"lamp\"]
}
```
We expect `action` to be an object: `{\"action\": {\"name\": \"turn_on\", \"params\": {...}}}`. The model is emitting a simplified form.

kevin m: This is the sanitization vs enforcement debate again. Current validator v2 marks simplified shapes as soft_reject when validator_mode=warn, hard_reject when validator_mode=enforce. Canary accidentally had enforce for 5% of traffic.

maria p: Oof. How did that happen?

sana r: Ops misconfigured the canary switch during rollout. We turned on enforce for a subset for latency measurements and forgot to flip it back to warn.

kevin m: Two problems we need to fix: (A) Console UX — users get an opaque 502 and can't see the raw model output to debug. (B) Billing/quotas — we billed tokens on hard_rejects; customers perceive it as 'charged for broken outputs'.

ton y l: Proposal for console: show a compact breadcrumb in the request detail that includes validator_status (ok|soft_reject|hard_reject), raw_output (collapsed with click-to-expand), and a diff against the expected contract. Add a hint: \"why this failed\" with one-line remediation.

maria p: For billing: we should issue an immediate credit for hard_rejects where final user did not receive a usable action. Implementation: add `final_delivery=false` and `reject_class=validator_enforce` to telemetry events and have the billing job zero those lines for the affected invoice period.

kevin m: Agrees but we need to be careful with fraud. We should only credit if `final_delivery=false` and `client_ack=false` from downstream delivery hooks. Also limit retrospective credits to 30 days.

maria p: Makes sense. Also want to surface coalesced metrics in the console: `soft_reject_rate_by_route`, `hard_reject_rate_by_model_variant`, `avg_validator_exec_ms`, `sampled_raw_payloads_link`.

kevin m: On routing: suggest a small change to fallback ordering for function hooks: try sanitizer_parser -> permissive_model_variant -> canonical_model_variant -> hard_fail. The idea being try quick sanitization before model switching to keep latency low.

tony l: Implementation idea: add `sanitizer: {enabled: true, max_ops: 3, attempts: 1}` where sanitizer runs light transforms (wrap scalars into expected objects, convert arrays to {items:...}, normalize keys). If sanitizer succeeds, mark `sanitized=true` and attach `sanitizer_patch` to telemetry.

kevin m: We'll need to add telemetry fields: `validator_mode` (warn|enforce), `sanitized` (true|false), `sanitizer_patch` (short string), `reject_class`, `final_delivery`, `client_ack`. Also expose these in the console filterable logs.

sana r: For rollout safety: can we enable sanitizer in canary with sampling=20% and validator_mode=warn for the rest? If sanitizer increases success rate and `sanitized=true` shows up in telemetry, we can flip more traffic. Also create an automatic rollback if `hard_reject_rate > 0.5%` for 5m.

maria p: I'll add a short playbook snippet: 1) If hard_reject_rate > 0.5% page oncall. 2) If sanitizer_coerced_rate > 2% for 1h, open a product incident to evaluate prompt/contract. 3) Billing credits automatically queued for manual review before issuing if total credits > $1000/day.

kevin m: I'll take the routing change PR. Tony, can you own sanitizer implementation and add minimal `sanitizer_patch` format? Sana, can you scope console changes to show raw_output collapsed and the new telemetry fields? Maria, can you own the billing playbook and backfill gating?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled 2026-03-26 01:30 UTC. Changes: validator_mode=warn(by-default), sanitizer_sampling=20% (canary), routing_order updated. Owners: kevin m, tony l. Link: https://deploys.internal/6531112222

maria p: Thanks all  I'll follow up with a short runbook and post canary metrics in 12h.
